newsitem.title: UK: EMAP shares up as NatWest raises to "buy".
newsitem.headline: EMAP shares up as NatWest raises to "buy".

text.p: Shares in British publishing group EMAP gained on Monday after NatWest Securities raised its recommendation to a "buy" from "add", market sources said.
EMAP shares rose as high as 713p in early trade before drifting back to 709p by 0952 GMT, up 13p or 1.86 percent on the day. The broader market was up 0.23 percent.
Market sources said the share was lifted by the NatWest recommendation. The stock has dropped sharply recently amid worries about a rift at management level.
Dealers said the stock was also lifted by reports the company is poised to make its first television acquisition.
The Sunday Telegraph reported that the company was planning to acquire cable music channel The Box for eight million stg this week. The Box is jointly-owned by TicketMaster and Video Jukebox Network.
The newspaper said the move was aimed at exploiting the youth market, and would be EMAP's second move in television. EMAP started Kiss TV in May, which supplies youth programming.
Neither Kiss TV nor The Box were likely to generate large advertising revenue in the short term, the report said, given the small audience figures for cable.
